1.web: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
1.asv: And when it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

2.web: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea; Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
2.asv: And embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail unto the places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

3.web: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
3.asv: And the next day we touched at Sidon: and Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him leave to go unto his friends and refresh himself.

4.web: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
4.asv: And putting to sea from thence, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

5.web: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
5.asv: And when we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

6.web: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.
6.asv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy; and he put us therein.

7.web: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
7.asv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and were come with difficulty over against Cnidus, the wind not further suffering us, we sailed under the lee of Crete, over against Salmone;

8.web: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
8.asv: and with difficulty coasting along it we came unto a certain place called Fair Havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

9.web: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them,
9.asv: And when much time was spent, and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast was now already gone by, Paul admonished them,

10.web: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”
10.asv: and said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the lading and the ship, but also of our lives.

11.web: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
11.asv: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship, than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

12.web: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking northeast and southeast.
12.asv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to put to sea from thence, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there; which is a haven of Crete, looking north-east and south-east.

13.web: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
13.asv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close in shore.

14.web: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.
14.asv: But after no long time there beat down from it a tempestuous wind, which is called Euraquilo:

15.web: When the ship was caught, and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven along.
15.asv: and when the ship was caught, and could not face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven.

16.web: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
16.asv: And running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat:

17.web: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.
17.asv: and when they had hoisted it up, they used helps, under-girding the ship; and, fearing lest they should be cast upon the Syrtis, they lowered the gear, and so were driven.

18.web: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.
18.asv: And as we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw the freight overboard;

19.web: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
19.asv: and the third day they cast out with their own hands the tackling of the ship.

20.web: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
20.asv: And when neither sun nor stars shone upon us for many days, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was now taken away.

21.web: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.
21.asv: And when they had been long without food, then Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.

22.web: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
22.asv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer; for there shall be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

23.web: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,
23.asv: For there stood by me this night an angel of the God whose I am, whom also I serve,

24.web: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
24.asv: saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must stand before Cæsar: and lo, God hath granted thee all them that sail with thee.

25.web: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
25.asv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even so as it hath been spoken unto me.

26.web: But we must run aground on a certain island.”
26.asv: But we must be cast upon a certain island.

27.web: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.
27.asv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven to and fro in the sea of Adria, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some country:

28.web: They took soundings, and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.
28.asv: and they sounded, and found twenty fathoms; and after a little space, they sounded again, and found fifteen fathoms.

29.web: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.
29.asv: And fearing lest haply we should be cast ashore on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for the day.

30.web: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,
30.asv: And as the sailors were seeking to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, under color as though they would lay out anchors from the foreship,

31.web: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”
31.asv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

32.web: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.
32.asv: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

33.web: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “This day is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
33.asv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take some food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

34.web: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”
34.asv: Wherefore I beseech you to take some food: for this is for your safety: for there shall not a hair perish from the head of any of you.

35.web: When he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and he broke it, and began to eat.
35.asv: And when he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; and he brake it, and began to eat.

36.web: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.
36.asv: Then were they all of good cheer, and themselves also took food.

37.web: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.
37.asv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

38.web: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
38.asv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

39.web: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.
39.asv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they perceived a certain bay with a beach, and they took counsel whether they could drive the ship upon it.

40.web: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
40.asv: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosing the bands of the rudders; and hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

41.web: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.
41.asv: But lighting upon a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground; and the foreship struck and remained unmoveable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

42.web: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.
42.asv: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

43.web: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;
43.asv: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stayed them from their purpose; and commanded that they who could swim should cast themselves overboard, and get first to the land;

44.web: and the rest should follow, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.
44.asv: and the rest, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. And so it came to pass, that they all escaped safe to the land.
